place_name: Fremont Peak (Marmot's Tooth pinnacle on the west face), Titcomb Basin, Wind River Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Titcomb Basin approach from Elkhart Park trailhead (Pole Creek, Seneca Lake, Indian Pass trails) to Titcomb Lakes; the Titcomb side trip alone starts at Island Lake, 1.6 mi to the foot of the basin
summit_or_glacier: pinnacle summit (rappel off); 12 pitches, Grade IV, on a 13,745 ft peak

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 1600 ft, 12 pitches, Grade IV; climbs a pinnacle on Fremont Peak's west face to its small summit.
Follow the Titcomb Basin approach to Titcomb Lakes, then head east past Mistake Lake.
From Elkhart Park Trailhead take the Pole Creek, Seneca Lake and Indian Pass trails into the basin.
Titcomb side trip from the Island Lake junction: foot of the basin at 1.6 mi, Upper Titcomb Lake about 3.6 mi.

note: Backcountry Wind River approach; no single trailhead-to-base mileage stated on the pages opened.

place_name: Okie's Thorn, satellite spire on the Grand Teton's East Ridge, Garnet Canyon, Grand Teton NP, Wyoming
approach_stated: Hike to JHMG Corbett High Camp, then north onto the Tepee Glacier to the base of the spire at Dike Col
summit_or_glacier: spire summit at 12,009 ft; approach crosses the Tepee Glacier

evidence.fact: Hike to JHMG Corbett High Camp and proceed north onto the Tepee Glacier to the base of the spire at Dike Col.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 360 ft, 4 pitches, Grade II; finishes in a notch on the SW side of the summit.

place_name: Spider Peak (12,234 ft), Ross Lakes Area, Wind River Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Trail Lake Ranch trailhead, about 8 miles on the Bomber Trail to Bomber Lake, then about an hour west/southwest on faint trails
summit_or_glacier: peak face, 8 pitches Grade IV; no glacier stated

evidence.fact: Hike about 8 miles on the Bomber Trail to Bomber Lake, then an hour up faint trails to Spider Peak.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 1000 ft, 8 pitches, Grade IV.

place_name: Watchtower, Cirque of the Towers, Wind River Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Cirque of the Towers approach (Big Sandy trailhead, over Jackass Pass), then 30-40 min from camp in the Cirque to the base
summit_or_glacier: tower (10,517 ft), 7 pitches Grade IV; no glacier stated

evidence.fact: Approach same as for the Cirque of the Towers; 30-40 min from camp in the Cirque to the base.
Drive to Big Sandy Campground; trail past Arrowhead Lake and up to the top of Jackass Pass.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 800 ft, 7 pitches, Grade IV.

note: The 30-40 min is from a backcountry camp, not from the car.

place_name: Pilot Peak, Absaroka Range (near Cooke City), Wyoming
approach_stated: Trail up Hayden Creek past Woody Falls, a couple of uphill miles to meadows; many parties high-camp in the West Basin

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 500 ft, 6 pitches, Grade III.
Hike past Woody Falls, a couple of uphill miles; many parties continue into the West Basin for a high camp.

note: Total approach length not stated; high camp customary.

place_name: Upper Blacktail Butte, Blacktail Butte, Grand Teton NP, Wyoming
approach_stated: From the Blacktail parking lot walk south on a well developed trail for 10-15 minutes

evidence.fact: From the Blacktail parking lot, walk south on a well developed trail for 10-15 minutes.
Closest MP match is stHank-O, 5.12c, Type: Sport, Alpine (no route named stHank-Hole listed).

note: Catalog name likely a misspelling of stHank-O; type taken from that page.

place_name: The Triple Traverse (Mt. Warren, Doublet, Dinwoody), Gannett Cirque / Dinwoody Glacier, Wind River Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Starts at Elsie Col; about an hour, maybe more, from the moraine (itself deep backcountry)
summit_or_glacier: traverse of three summits; glacier travel, descent across the glacier

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine, Grade IV; day-long traverse of Mt. Warren, Doublet and Dinwoody; climbers must be glacier rigged.

place_name: Boy Scout Cirque (Treasure Boulders), Teton Canyon, Wyoming
approach_stated: 1 hour approach time with 300 m vertical gain (area figure, for the big-wall routes); the boulders are on the east side via a trail from the Scout Camp bridge
summit_or_glacier: no; dolomite boulders/top-rope blocks among trees

evidence.fact: 1 hour approach time with 300 m vertical gain.
Type: TR, Alpine, 30 ft; dolomite boulders among Douglas fir and aspen with top-rope climbs and boulder problems.

note: Stated 1 hour sits exactly at the 60-min limit; 30 ft top-rope blocks, no summit.

place_name: The Mouth (of the Clark's Fork), Clarks Fork Canyon, Absaroka Range, Wyoming
approach_stated: Walk a quarter to half a mile from the highway, crossing a BLM fence, to reach the routes
summit_or_glacier: no; canyon wall, descent by 7 rappels

evidence.fact: Walk a quarter to half a mile from the highway, crossing a BLM fence, to reach the routes.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 650 ft, 7 pitches, Grade II; descent 7x 40 m raps.

place_name: The Evolution Wall, Hallway of the Gods, Pillars of Creation, 'The Others', Tahquitz & Suicide Rocks (San Jacinto Mtns), California
approach_stated: No time or distance stated; best approach probably Devil's Slide Trail, then cross-country and down a descent gully; parent area says 'Mucho hiking'
summit_or_glacier: no; 1-2 pitch formations at about 8,300 ft

evidence.fact: Among the most difficult formations to reach; best approach probably Devil's Slide Trail, then cross-country south and down a gully.
Approach section says only: Mucho hiking.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 200 ft, 2 pitches, Grade II; hand crack to chimney on the Evolution Wall.

note: Approach plainly long (trail then cross-country) but no figure stated on pages opened; leans alpine by approach, though the routes are short cragging.

place_name: Columbine Peak (12,668 ft), Palisades, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: South Lake trailhead, up the Bishop Pass trail to Bishop Pass; route on the Dusy Basin side of Knapsack Pass
summit_or_glacier: peak face; may continue to the summit (unconfirmed); no glacier stated

evidence.fact: Take the road to the South Lake trailhead and hike the Bishop Pass trail to Bishop Pass.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 600 ft, 5 pitches, Grade III; on the Dusy Basin side of Knapsack Pass.

note: Approach crosses Bishop Pass; no mileage stated.

place_name: Bear Creek Spire (13,713 ft), Little Lakes Valley, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: Mosquito Flat trailhead, Little Lakes Valley trail to Long Lake then to Dade Lake: 4.25 miles, 1,300 ft gain

evidence.fact: Hike Little Lakes Valley trail to Long Lake and up to Dade Lake (4.25 miles, 1,300 feet of elevation gain).
Type: Trad, Alpine, 22 pitches, Grade IV; approach from Mosquito Flat via Morgan Pass trail toward Gem Lakes and Dade Lake.

place_name: Aiguille Junior (13,927 ft), Whitney area, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: Via the Mt Whitney Trail to Trail Camp, then northwest from Trail Camp
summit_or_glacier: summit (corner system leads directly to the summit), 6 pitches Grade III

evidence.fact: Approach via the Mt Whitney Trail, then head NW from Trail Camp.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 1000 ft, 6 pitches, Grade III; the big corner system leads directly to the summit.

note: Trail Camp is a Whitney-trail backcountry camp; mileage not stated on the pages opened.

place_name: Mt Barnard East Peak (Peak 13,680+), Whitney area, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: From camp at the tarn, about 60-90 minutes across talus to the base; FA party describes a 6,000-foot approach
summit_or_glacier: top of the pillar/summit, 10 pitches Grade IV; perched snowfield below the wall

evidence.fact: Type: Trad, Alpine, 1500 ft, 10 pitches, Grade IV; approach about 60-90 minutes from camp across talus.
Rowell's 1973 account: loads carried up the arduous 6000-foot approach; reached the top at 5:30 P.M.

place_name: Crystal Crag (Other Alpine Routes), Lake George, Mammoth Lakes, California
approach_stated: Lake George parking lot, Crystal Lake Trail and climbers' trail; the approach takes about 45 minutes
summit_or_glacier: snow route (Mod. Snow) to the summit; descent West Face or South Ridge 3rd class

evidence.fact: Park at Lake George, hike the Crystal Lake Trail; the approach takes about 45 minutes.
Type: Trad, Snow, Alpine, 300 ft, Grade II; upper snowfield then roughly straight to the summit.

note: Short (45 min) approach but a snow route finishing on the summit, so alpine by the summit/snow rule.

place_name: The Turret, Little Slide Spires, Sawtooth Ridge (Twin Lakes), High Sierra, California
approach_stated: Twin Lakes campground, Robinson Creek Trail about 2.5 miles to the mouth of Little Slide Canyon, then up the canyon past a cliff band
summit_or_glacier: summit spire, 9 pitches Grade III; descent 1-2 hours back to the base

evidence.fact: Robinson Creek Trail about 2.5 miles to the mouth of Little Slide Canyon; spires sit farther up the canyon.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 800 ft, 9 pitches, Grade III; pitch 10 reaches the summit spire; 1-2 hours descent to base.

place_name: Bedayan Minaret (11,390 ft), Ritter Range / Minarets, High Sierra, California
approach_stated: Agnew Meadows trailhead, Shadow Creek Trail 6.8 miles to Iceberg Lake (camp), then about 400 ft of steepening snow to the base
summit_or_glacier: ridge to summit, 10 pitches; permanent snowfield on approach and descent

evidence.fact: Hike the Shadow Creek Trail 6.8 miles to Iceberg Lake; ascend about 400 feet of steepening snow to the base.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 1600 ft, 10 pitches, Grade III; total descent about 3 hours to Iceberg Lake.

place_name: Emigrant Labor, near Piute Lake, Emigrant Wilderness (Sonora Pass Hwy 108), California
approach_stated: Crabtree Trailhead near Pinecrest; 'hiked for several miles before seeing any major rock features'; route is just north of Piute Lake

evidence.fact: Accessed at the Crabtree Trailhead near Pinecrest; hiked several miles before seeing any major rock features.
Type: Trad, Alpine, 450 ft, 4 pitches; just north of Piute Lake, worth having carried your gear all that way.

note: Roadless wilderness approach of several miles.

place_name: Dome of the Immaculate Conception (Notre Dome), Courtright Reservoir, Hwy 168, Western Sierra, California
approach_stated: Off Courtright Road, 0.75 mile on a logging spur to a campsite, then hike NW, contour a ridge, cross Short Hair Creek and climb talus; no time stated
summit_or_glacier: no; granite slab dome, 100 ft route

evidence.fact: 0.75 mile on logging spur to a campsite; hike NW, contour around a ridge, cross Short Hair Creek, climb talus to the base.
Type: Trad, 100 ft (MP does not tag it Alpine).

note: Road-accessed slab near Courtright Reservoir; likely a short approach, but no time or foot distance stated.
